subject: Shared fabric decommission plan + control/data split validation
messages:
From: Amar Singh <amar@heliosys.com>

Cc: Lin Zhao <lin.zhao@heliosys.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Shared fabric decommission plan + initial diagrams

Mina,

Thanks again for hopping on the call this morning. As discussed, Helio is planning to decommission our legacy shared network fabric and migrate tenant traffic to dedicated VPC attachments into Redwood's on-prem control/data split design. Primary asks from our side:

- Validate the proposed control-plane relay points in the attached diagram (shared-fabric-decommission-diagram-v2.png).
- Confirm canary rollout steps so we don't impact inference latency for production tenants.
- A short runbook for failback if the first wave shows increased tail latency.

I've attached the current topology and a CSV of tenant mappings (controlplane-dataflow-table.csv). Can we get a short readout from your ops/arch team by tomorrow EOD PT?

Appreciate it —
Amar Singh
Director, Cloud Architecture | Helio Systems
amar@heliosys.com | +1 415 555 0198

Attachments: shared-fabric-decommission-diagram-v2.png (image/png), controlplane-dataflow-table.csv (text/csv)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Amar Singh <amar@heliosys.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shared fabric decommission plan + initial diagrams

Amar — thanks for the packet. Quick read-through notes and next steps below. High-level: we can support the decommission provided Helio accepts two operational constraints (canary segmentation + sticky control-plane endpoints during KV-cache warmup).

Immediate items for validation:
- Control-plane relay points: the diagram looks OK but we need the AS-path for tenant subnets on the two east clusters (diagram callout A/B). Can you confirm BGP tags?
- Canary policy: recommend 5% of tenants (small, low-traffic) for 48h with auto-fallback thresholds (see canary-runbook-ops.md).
- Observability: we need token-level tracing enabled for the canary tenants and 1s granularity p95 metrics for token latency.

Risks:
- KV-cache cold starts will show a 30–60ms tail for first 5k tokens if we redirect control-plane to new relays; we mitigate with warmup prefix caching as part of the canary.
- Egress policy mismatch can cause occasional SYN retries in the first 2 hours after cutover; Neha, please ensure ops has the NAT keepalive recipe.

I'll loop in Jonas and Karthik for the on-prem routing constraints and runbook text. We'll produce a short acceptance checklist and a 1-page failback plan by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: canary-runbook-ops.md (text/markdown)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Amar Singh <amar@heliosys.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shared fabric decommission plan + control/data split validation

Adding a couple of operational constraints from infra:

1) Control-plane affinity: during the canary we must pin control-plane sessions to the same relay pair for at least 12 hours to avoid KV-cache thrashing. We'll publish a short-lived affinity token for Helio to honor.

2) MTU/fragmentation: the new path shows a 1400 MTU on the edge hop; if any tenant uses >1200 tokenized payloads we should enable jumbo-fragment handling. Karthik, can we get the kernel-side iptables rule and a README snippet?

3) Rollback triggers: we'll set an automatic rollback on any of the following for a canary cohort: p95 token latency +25% vs baseline, error rate >0.8%, or a sustained 3x increase in autoretry counts.

Neha — please add the NAT keepalive and BFD probe thresholds to the runbook. Amar — we should set a 3-hour maintenance window for the initial cut so we have a clean alerting baseline.

-Jonas
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Thanks — helpful. We can provide AS-paths and BGP tags by COB today. We also agree to the 3-hour maintenance window for the first cut (proposed 02:00–05:00 PT Saturday).

A couple of clarifications:
- For control-plane affinity token, does Redwood issue the token and our edge will honor it, or do you require us to set an explicit session pin via BGP communities?
- MTU: we have jumbo enabled on the pod fabric; we will cross-check with tenant teams to ensure payloads don't exceed the safe window.

We'll upload the AS-path CSV to the Drive folder and flag the tenant list with suggested canary cohort candidates (low QPS).

—Amar

Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shared fabric decommission plan + control/data split validation — ops artifacts attached

Amar / team — quick technical answers and artifacts attached inline in the Drive folder. Short answers below: 

- Affinity token: Redwood will mint a time-limited affinity token (JWT) and we will provide a BGP-community fallback. The token is preferred (less brittle) — we'll put both methods in the runbook.
- iptables/jumbo-policy: attached snippet in the Drive (README_jumbo_fragment.md) — requires a single kernel sysctl and a DNAT rule on the edge NAT.
- BFD thresholds and NAT keepalive: added to canary-runbook-ops.md (probe interval 100ms, detect-mult 3).

Action items assigned: 
- Helio (Amar): provide AS-path map + flag canary tenants (COB today) — owner: Amar Singh
- Redwood (Neha): finalize runbook and add failure play (failback route + TTL flush) — owner: Neha Kapoor — due EOD tomorrow
- Redwood (Jonas/Karthik): produce kernel snippets and canary monitoring dashboard (p95, retry-rate) — due +48h

I'll add the artifacts to the Drive and send a short readout once the Helio AS-paths land.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Software Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
